<h1 id="opensearch-api-specification-default">Default</h1>

## info.0

<a id="opIdinfo.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /`

Returns basic information about the cluster.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="info0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cluster_name": "string",
  "cluster_uuid": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "tagline": "string",
  "version": {
    "build_date": "string",
    "build_flavor": "string",
    "build_hash": "string",
    "build_snapshot": true,
    "build_type": "string",
    "distribution": "string",
    "lucene_version": "string",
    "minimum_index_compatibility_version": "string",
    "minimum_wire_compatibility_version": "string",
    "number": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="info0-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="info0-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_name|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|none|The name of a resource or configuration element.|
|cluster_uuid|[_common___Uuid](#schema_common___uuid)|true|none|The universally unique identifier.|
|name|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|none|The name of a resource or configuration element.|
|tagline|string|true|none|none|
|version|[_common___OpenSearchVersionInfo](#schema_common___opensearchversioninfo)|true|none|The version information for OpenSearch.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## ping.0

<a id="opIdping.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/ \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /`

Returns whether the cluster is running.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="ping0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="ping0-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## indices.get_alias.0

<a id="opIdindices.get_alias.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_alias \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_alias`

Returns an alias.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/im-plugin/index-alias/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesgetalias0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.<br>Valid values are: `all`, `open`, `closed`, `hidden`, `none`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alias|body|string|false|none|
|» filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» index|body|string|false|none|
|» index_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_write_index|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.<br>If an alias points to multiple indexes or data streams and `is_write_index` isn't set, the alias rejects write requests.<br>If an index alias points to one index and `is_write_index` isn't set, the index automatically acts as the write index.<br>Data stream aliases don't automatically set a write data stream, even if the alias points to one data stream.|
|» routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» search_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_hidden|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the alias will be hidden`.|

## indices.get_alias.1

<a id="opIdindices.get_alias.1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_alias/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_alias/{name}`

Returns an alias.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/im-plugin/index-alias/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesgetalias1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|true|A comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.<br>Valid values are: `all`, `open`, `closed`, `hidden`, `none`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="indicesputalias2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|Alias to update.<br>If the alias doesn't exist, the request creates it.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alias|body|string|false|none|
|» filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» index|body|string|false|none|
|» index_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_write_index|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.<br>If an alias points to multiple indexes or data streams and `is_write_index` isn't set, the alias rejects write requests.<br>If an index alias points to one index and `is_write_index` isn't set, the index automatically acts as the write index.<br>Data stream aliases don't automatically set a write data stream, even if the alias points to one data stream.|
|» routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» search_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_hidden|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the alias will be hidden`.|

```json
}
```

<h3 id="indicesputalias1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|Alias to update.<br>If the alias doesn't exist, the request creates it.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alias|body|string|false|none|
|» filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» index|body|string|false|none|
|» index_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_write_index|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.<br>If an alias points to multiple indexes or data streams and `is_write_index` isn't set, the alias rejects write requests.<br>If an index alias points to one index and `is_write_index` isn't set, the index automatically acts as the write index.<br>Data stream aliases don't automatically set a write data stream, even if the alias points to one data stream.|
|» routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» search_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_hidden|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the alias will be hidden`.|

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
```

`HEAD /_alias/{name}`

Returns information about whether a particular alias exists.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesexistsalias0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|true|A comma-separated list of aliases to check. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.<br>Valid values are: `all`, `open`, `closed`, `hidden`, `none`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, requests that include a missing data stream or index in the target indexes or data streams return an error.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="indicesexistsalias0-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|
|404|Not Found||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="indicesputalias4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|Alias to update.<br>If the alias doesn't exist, the request creates it.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alias|body|string|false|none|
|» filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» index|body|string|false|none|
|» index_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_write_index|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.<br>If an alias points to multiple indexes or data streams and `is_write_index` isn't set, the alias rejects write requests.<br>If an index alias points to one index and `is_write_index` isn't set, the index automatically acts as the write index.<br>Data stream aliases don't automatically set a write data stream, even if the alias points to one data stream.|
|» routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» search_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_hidden|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the alias will be hidden`.|

<h3 id="indicesputalias3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|Alias to update.<br>If the alias doesn't exist, the request creates it.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alias|body|string|false|none|
|» filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» index|body|string|false|none|
|» index_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_write_index|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.<br>If an alias points to multiple indexes or data streams and `is_write_index` isn't set, the alias rejects write requests.<br>If an index alias points to one index and `is_write_index` isn't set, the index automatically acts as the write index.<br>Data stream aliases don't automatically set a write data stream, even if the alias points to one data stream.|
|» routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» search_routing|body|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|The routing value for the document.|
|» is_hidden|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the alias will be hidden`.|

## indices.analyze.0

<a id="opIdindices.analyze.0"></a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_analyze \

    "text": "string",
    "tokenizer": "string"
  }'
```

`GET /_analyze`

Performs the analysis process on a text and return the tokens breakdown of the text.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/analyze-apis/perform-text-analysis/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "analyzer": "string",
  "attributes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "char_filter": [
    "string"
  ],
  "explain": true,
  "field": "string",
  "filter": [
    "string"
  ],
  "normalizer": "string",
  "text": "string",
  "tokenizer": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="indicesanalyze0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|query|string|false|The name of the index to scope the operation.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» analyzer|body|string|false|The name of the analyzer that should be applied to the provided `text`.<br>This could be a built-in analyzer, or an analyzer that's been configured in the index.|
|» attributes|body|[string]|false|Array of token attributes used to filter the output of the `explain` parameter.|
|» char_filter|body|[[_common.analysis___CharFilter](#schema_common.analysis___charfilter)]|false|Array of character filters used to preprocess characters before the tokenizer.|
|» explain|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes token attributes and additional details.|
|» field|body|[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)|false|The path to a field or an array of paths. Some APIs support wildcards in the path, which allows you to select multiple fields.|
|» filter|body|[[_common.analysis___TokenFilter](#schema_common.analysis___tokenfilter)]|false|Array of token filters used to apply after the tokenizer.|
|» normalizer|body|string|false|Normalizer to use to convert text into a single token.|
|» text|body|[indices.analyze___TextToAnalyze](#schemaindices.analyze___texttoanalyze)|false|none|
|» tokenizer|body|[_common.analysis___Tokenizer](#schema_common.analysis___tokenizer)|false|none|

`GET /_cluster/allocation/explain`

Explains how shards are allocated in the current cluster and provides an explanation for why unassigned shards can't be allocated to a node.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-allocation/">External documentation</a>

```json
{
  "current_node": "string",
  "index": "string",
  "primary": true,
  "shard": 0
}
```

<h3 id="clusterallocationexplain0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_disk_info|query|boolean|false|When `true`, returns information about disk usage and shard sizes.|
|include_yes_decisions|query|boolean|false|When `true`, returns any `YES` decisions in the allocation explanation. `YES` decisions indicate when a particular shard allocation attempt was successful for the given node.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» current_node|body|string|false|Specifies the node ID or the name of the node to only explain a shard that is currently located on the specified node.|
|» index|body|[_common___IndexName](#schema_common___indexname)|false|none|
|» primary|body|boolean|false|When `true`, returns a routing explanation for the primary shard based on the node ID.|
|» shard|body|integer(int32)|false|Specifies the ID of the shard that you would like an explanation for.|

## cluster.stats.0

`GET /_cluster/stats`

Returns a high-level overview of cluster statistics.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-stats/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clusterstats0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Whether to return settings in the flat form, which can improve readability, especially for heavily nested settings.<br>For example, the flat form of `"cluster": { "max_shards_per_node": 500 }` is `"cluster.max_shards_per_node": "500"`.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for each node to respond.<br>If a node does not respond before its timeout expires, the response does not include its stats.<br>However, timed out nodes are included in the response's `_nodes.failed` property. Defaults to no timeout.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="clusterstats0-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_nodes|[_common___NodeStatistics](#schema_common___nodestatistics)|false|none|Contains statistics about the number of nodes selected by the request's node filters.|
|cluster_name|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|none|The name of the cluster.|
|cluster_uuid|[_common___Uuid](#schema_common___uuid)|true|none|The unique identifier of the cluster.|
|indices|[cluster.stats___ClusterIndices](#schemacluster.stats___clusterindices)|false|none|Displays statistics about indexes in the cluster.|
|nodes|[cluster.stats___ClusterNodes](#schemacluster.stats___clusternodes)|false|none|Displays statistics about nodes selected by the request's node filters.|
|status|[_common___HealthStatus](#schema_common___healthstatus)|true|none|The health status of the cluster, based on the state of its primary and replica shards.|
|timestamp|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The Unix timestamp, in milliseconds, indicating when any cluster statistics were last refreshed.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## cluster.stats.3

<a id="opIdcluster.stats.3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/stats/_all/_all/nodes/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/stats/{metric}/{index_metric}/nodes/{node_id}`

Returns a high-level overview of cluster statistics.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-stats/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clusterstats3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_metric|path|[[cluster.stats___IndexMetric](#schemacluster.stats___indexmetric)]|true|A comma-separated list of [index metric groups](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-stats/#index-metric-groups), for example, `docs,store`.|
|metric|path|[[cluster.stats___Metric](#schemacluster.stats___metric)]|true|Limit the information returned to the specified metrics.|
|node_id|path|[_common___NodeIds](#schema_common___nodeids)|true|none|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Whether to return settings in the flat form, which can improve readability, especially for heavily nested settings.<br>For example, the flat form of `"cluster": { "max_shards_per_node": 500 }` is `"cluster.max_shards_per_node": "500"`.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for each node to respond.<br>If a node does not respond before its timeout expires, the response does not include its stats.<br>However, timed out nodes are included in the response's `_nodes.failed` property. Defaults to no timeout.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

## cluster.stats.2

<a id="opIdcluster.stats.2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/stats/_all/nodes/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/stats/{metric}/nodes/{node_id}`

Returns a high-level overview of cluster statistics.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-stats/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clusterstats2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric|path|[[cluster.stats___Metric](#schemacluster.stats___metric)]|true|Limit the information returned to the specified metrics.|
|node_id|path|[_common___NodeIds](#schema_common___nodeids)|true|none|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Whether to return settings in the flat form, which can improve readability, especially for heavily nested settings.<br>For example, the flat form of `"cluster": { "max_shards_per_node": 500 }` is `"cluster.max_shards_per_node": "500"`.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for each node to respond.<br>If a node does not respond before its timeout expires, the response does not include its stats.<br>However, timed out nodes are included in the response's `_nodes.failed` property. Defaults to no timeout.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

|metric|indices|
|metric|ingest|

|metric|os|

|metric|plugins|
|metric|process|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="clusterstats1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_nodes|[_common___NodeStatistics](#schema_common___nodestatistics)|false|none|Contains statistics about the number of nodes selected by the request's node filters.|
|cluster_name|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|none|The name of the cluster.|
|cluster_uuid|[_common___Uuid](#schema_common___uuid)|true|none|The unique identifier of the cluster.|
|indices|[cluster.stats___ClusterIndices](#schemacluster.stats___clusterindices)|false|none|Displays statistics about indexes in the cluster.|
|nodes|[cluster.stats___ClusterNodes](#schemacluster.stats___clusternodes)|false|none|Displays statistics about nodes selected by the request's node filters.|
|status|[_common___HealthStatus](#schema_common___healthstatus)|true|none|The health status of the cluster, based on the state of its primary and replica shards.|
|timestamp|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The Unix timestamp, in milliseconds, indicating when any cluster statistics were last refreshed.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## cluster.post_voting_config_exclusions.0

<a id="opIdcluster.post_voting_config_exclusions.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/voting_config_exclusions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`

Updates the cluster voting configuration by excluding certain node IDs or names.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clusterpostvotingconfigexclusions0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_ids|query|[_common___Ids](#schema_common___ids)|false|A comma-separated list of node IDs to exclude<br>from the voting configuration. When using this setting, you cannot also specify `node_names`. Either `node_ids` or `node_names` are required to receive a valid response.|
|node_names|query|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|false|A comma-separated list of node names to exclude from the<br>voting configuration. When using this setting, you cannot also specify `node_ids`. Either `node_ids` or `node_names` are required to receive a valid response.|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|When adding a voting configuration exclusion, the API waits for the<br>specified nodes to be excluded from the voting configuration before<br>returning a response. If the timeout expires before the appropriate condition<br>is satisfied, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="clusterpostvotingconfigexclusions0-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## cluster.delete_voting_config_exclusions.0

<a id="opIdcluster.delete_voting_config_exclusions.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/voting_config_exclusions \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`

Clears any cluster voting configuration exclusions.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clusterdeletevotingconfigexclusions0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|wait_for_removal|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to wait for all excluded nodes to be removed from the<br>cluster before clearing the voting configuration exclusions list.<br>When `true`, all excluded nodes are removed from<br>the cluster before this API takes any action. When `false`, the<br>voting configuration exclusions list is cleared even if some excluded<br>nodes are still in the cluster.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="clusterdeletevotingconfigexclusions0-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## cluster.get_component_template.0

<a id="opIdcluster.get_component_template.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_component_template`

Returns one or more component templates.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clustergetcomponenttemplate0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for a response from the cluster manager node. For more information about supported time units, see [Common parameters](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/common-parameters/#time-units).|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Whether to return settings in the flat form, which can improve readability, especially for heavily nested settings.<br>For example, the flat form of `"cluster": { "max_shards_per_node": 500 }` is `"cluster.max_shards_per_node": "500"`.|
|local|query|boolean|false|When `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>When `false`, information is retrieved from the cluster manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

</aside>

## cluster.get_component_template.1

<a id="opIdcluster.get_component_template.1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_component_template/{name}`

Returns one or more component templates.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="clustergetcomponenttemplate1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|The name of the component template to retrieve.<br>Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for a response from the cluster manager node. For more information about supported time units, see [Common parameters](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/common-parameters/#time-units).|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Whether to return settings in the flat form, which can improve readability, especially for heavily nested settings.<br>For example, the flat form of `"cluster": { "max_shards_per_node": 500 }` is `"cluster.max_shards_per_node": "500"`.|
|local|query|boolean|false|When `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>When `false`, information is retrieved from the cluster manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="clusterputcomponenttemplate1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|The name of the component template to create.<br>OpenSearch includes the following built-in component templates: `logs-mappings`, `logs-settings`, `metrics-mappings`, `metrics-settings`, `synthetics-mapping`, and `synthetics-settings`.<br>OpenSearch uses these templates to configure backing indexes for its data streams.<br>If you want to overwrite one of these templates, set the replacement template `version` to a higher value than the current version.<br>If you want to disable all built-in component and index templates, set `stack.templates.enabled` to `false` using the [Cluster Update Settings API](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-settings/).|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for a response from the cluster manager node. For more information about supported time units, see [Common parameters](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/common-parameters/#time-units).|
|create|query|boolean|false|When `true`, this request cannot replace or update existing component templates.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|This setting overrides the `action.auto_create_index` cluster setting.<br>When set to `true` in a component template, indexes are automatically created using that<br>template. When set to `false`, data streams matching the component template must always be explicitly created.|
|» template|body|[indices._common___IndexState](#schemaindices._common___indexstate)|true|The state configuration of an index.|
|» version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» _meta|body|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|

<h3 id="clusterputcomponenttemplate0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|The name of the component template to create.<br>OpenSearch includes the following built-in component templates: `logs-mappings`, `logs-settings`, `metrics-mappings`, `metrics-settings`, `synthetics-mapping`, and `synthetics-settings`.<br>OpenSearch uses these templates to configure backing indexes for its data streams.<br>If you want to overwrite one of these templates, set the replacement template `version` to a higher value than the current version.<br>If you want to disable all built-in component and index templates, set `stack.templates.enabled` to `false` using the [Cluster Update Settings API](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/cluster-api/cluster-settings/).|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|The amount of time to wait for a response from the cluster manager node. For more information about supported time units, see [Common parameters](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/api-reference/common-parameters/#time-units).|
|create|query|boolean|false|When `true`, this request cannot replace or update existing component templates.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|This setting overrides the `action.auto_create_index` cluster setting.<br>When set to `true` in a component template, indexes are automatically created using that<br>template. When set to `false`, data streams matching the component template must always be explicitly created.|
|» template|body|[indices._common___IndexState](#schemaindices._common___indexstate)|true|The state configuration of an index.|
|» version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» _meta|body|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|

<h3 id="count0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|If `true`, wildcard and prefix queries are analyzed.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|analyzer|query|string|false|Analyzer to use for the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|default_operator|query|[_common.query_dsl___Operator](#schema_common.query_dsl___operator)|false|The default operator for query string query: `AND` or `OR`.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|df|query|string|false|Field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|none|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|If `true`, concrete, expanded or aliased indexes are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.|
|lenient|query|boolean|false|If `true`, format-based query failures (such as providing text to a numeric field) in the query string will be ignored.|
|min_score|query|number(float)|false|Sets the minimum `_score` value that documents must have to be included in the result.|
|preference|query|string|false|Specifies the node or shard the operation should be performed on.<br>Random by default.|
|q|query|string|false|Query in the Lucene query string syntax.|
|routing|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.|
|terminate_after|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.<br>If a query reaches this limit, OpenSearch terminates the query early.<br>OpenSearch collects documents before sorting.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» query|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|default_operator|and|
|default_operator|AND|
|default_operator|or|
|default_operator|OR|

## delete_by_query_rethrottle.0

<a id="opIddelete_by_query_rethrottle.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_delete_by_query/string/_rethrottle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_delete_by_query/{task_id}/_rethrottle`

Changes the number of requests per second for a particular Delete By Query operation.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="deletebyqueryrethrottle0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_id|path|[_common___TaskId](#schema_common___taskid)|true|The ID for the task.|
|requests_per_second|query|number(float)|false|The throttle for this request in sub-requests per second.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

<h3 id="fieldcaps0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias,<br>or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes. This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes. For example, a request<br>targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with foo but no index starts with bar.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|The type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|fields|query|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to retrieve capabilities for. Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `true`, missing or closed indexes are not included in the response.|
|include_unmapped|query|boolean|false|If `true`, unmapped fields are included in the response.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» fields|body|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|» index_filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|

<h3 id="fieldcaps1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias,<br>or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes. This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes. For example, a request<br>targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with foo but no index starts with bar.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|The type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|fields|query|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to retrieve capabilities for. Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `true`, missing or closed indexes are not included in the response.|
|include_unmapped|query|boolean|false|If `true`, unmapped fields are included in the response.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» fields|body|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|» index_filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|

## indices.flush.0

<a id="opIdindices.flush.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_flush \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_flush`

Performs the flush operation on one or more indexes.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesflush0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.<br>Valid values are: `all`, `open`, `closed`, `hidden`, `none`.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request forces a flush even if there are no changes to commit to the index.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.|
|wait_if_ongoing|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the flush operation blocks until execution when another flush operation is running.<br>If `false`, OpenSearch returns an error if you request a flush when another flush operation is running.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

## indices.flush.1

<a id="opIdindices.flush.1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_flush \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_flush`

Performs the flush operation on one or more indexes.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesflush1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indexes.<br>This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indexes.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.<br>Valid values are: `all`, `open`, `closed`, `hidden`, `none`.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request forces a flush even if there are no changes to commit to the index.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.|
|wait_if_ongoing|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the flush operation blocks until execution when another flush operation is running.<br>If `false`, OpenSearch returns an error if you request a flush when another flush operation is running.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_shards": {
    "failed": 0,
    "successful": 0,
    "total": 0,
    "failures": [
      {
        "shard": 0,
        "index": "string",
        "node": "string",
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "reason": "string",
          "stack_trace": "string",
          "caused_by": {},
          "root_cause": [
            {}
          ],
          "suppressed": [
            {}
          ],
          "header": {
            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          },
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        }
      }
    ],
    "skipped": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="indicesflush1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_common___ShardsOperationResponseBase](#schema_common___shardsoperationresponsebase)|

## indices.forcemerge.0

<a id="opIdindices.forcemerge.0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_forcemerge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_forcemerge`

Performs the force merge operation on one or more indexes.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesforcemerge0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|Whether to ignore if a wildcard indexes expression resolves into no concrete indexes. (This includes `_all` string or when no indexes have been specified)|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_common___ExpandWildcards](#schema_common___expandwildcards)|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indexes that are open, closed or both.|
|flush|query|boolean|false|Specify whether the index should be flushed after performing the operation.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|Whether specified concrete indexes should be ignored when unavailable (missing or closed)|
|max_num_segments|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of larger segments into which smaller segments are merged.<br>Set this parameter to 1 to merge all segments into one segment.<br>The default behavior is to perform the merge as necessary.|
|only_expunge_deletes|query|boolean|false|Specify whether the operation should only expunge deleted documents|
|primary_only|query|boolean|false|Specify whether the operation should only perform on primary shards. Defaults to false.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|Should the request wait until the force merge is completed.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_shards": {
    "failed": 0,
    "successful": 0,
    "total": 0,
    "failures": [
      {
        "shard": 0,
        "index": "string",
        "node": "string",
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "reason": "string",
          "stack_trace": "string",
          "caused_by": {},
          "root_cause": [
            {}
          ],
          "suppressed": [
            {}
          ],
          "header": {
            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          },
          "property1": null,
          "property2": null
        }
      }
    ],
    "skipped": 0
  },
  "task": "string"
}
```

|200|OK||Inline|

|cause|query|string|false|User defined reason for dry-run creating the new template for simulation purposes.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|create|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the template passed in the body is only used if no existing templates match the same index patterns. If `false`, the simulation uses the template with the highest priority. Note that the template is not permanently added or updated in either case; it is only used for the simulation.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplate](#schemaindices._common___indextemplate)|false|none|
|» index_patterns|body|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|true|A comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve. Supports wildcards (`*`).  To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|» composed_of|body|[[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)]|false|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|» template|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplateSummary](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatesummary)|false|The summary configuration for an index template.|
|» version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» priority|body|integer(int64)|false|The priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by OpenSearch.|
|» _meta|body|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the template allows automatic index creation.|
|» data_stream|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplateDataStreamConfiguration](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatedatastreamconfiguration)|false|The data stream configuration for an index template.|

<h3 id="indicessimulateindextemplate0-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|Index or template name to simulate|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node. If no response is received<br>before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|This setting overrides the value of the `action.auto_create_index` cluster setting.<br>If set to `true` in a template, then indexes can be automatically created using that template even if auto-creation of indexes is disabled using `actions.auto_create_index`.<br>If set to `false`, then indexes or data streams matching the template must always be explicitly created, and may never be automatically created.|
|» index_patterns|body|[_common___Indices](#schema_common___indices)|false|A comma-separated list of data streams, indexes, and aliases used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indexes, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|» composed_of|body|[[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)]|false|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|» template|body|[indices.put_index_template___IndexTemplateMapping](#schemaindices.put_index_template___indextemplatemapping)|false|none|
|» data_stream|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplateDataStreamConfiguration](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatedatastreamconfiguration)|false|The data stream configuration for an index template.|
|» priority|body|integer|false|Priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by OpenSearch.|
|» version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» _meta|body|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|

<h3 id="indicessimulatetemplate1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|The name of the index template to simulate. To test a template configuration before you add it to the cluster, omit<br>this parameter and specify the template configuration in the request body.|
|cause|query|string|false|User defined reason for dry-run creating the new template for simulation purposes.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|create|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the template passed in the body is only used if no existing templates match the same index patterns. If `false`, the simulation uses the template with the highest priority. Note that the template is not permanently added or updated in either case; it is only used for the simulation.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplate](#schemaindices._common___indextemplate)|false|none|
|» index_patterns|body|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|true|A comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve. Supports wildcards (`*`).  To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|» composed_of|body|[[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)]|false|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|» template|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplateSummary](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatesummary)|false|The summary configuration for an index template.|
|» version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» priority|body|integer(int64)|false|The priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by OpenSearch.|
|» _meta|body|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the template allows automatic index creation.|
|» data_stream|body|[indices._common___IndexTemplateDataStreamConfiguration](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatedatastreamconfiguration)|false|The data stream configuration for an index template.|

## indices.get_index_template.1

<a id="opIdindices.get_index_template.1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_index_template/{name}`

Returns an index template.

<a href="https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/im-plugin/index-templates/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="indicesgetindextemplate1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)|true|The name of the index template to retrieve. Wildcard (*) expressions are supported.|
|cluster_manager_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|Operation timeout for connection to cluster-manager node.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns settings in flat format.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only. Defaults to false, which means information is retrieved from the cluster-manager node.|
|master_timeout|query|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|**Deprecated.** Period to wait for a connection to the cluster-manager node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
