|» collapse|body|[_core.search___FieldCollapse](#schema_core.search___fieldcollapse)|false|none|
|» explain|body|boolean|false|If `true`, returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.|
|» ext|body|object|false|Configuration of search extensions defined by OpenSearch plugins.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» from|body|number|false|Starting document offset.<br>Needs to be non-negative.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|» highlight|body|[_core.search___Highlight](#schema_core.search___highlight)|false|none|
|» track_total_hits|body|[_core.search___TrackHits](#schema_core.search___trackhits)|false|The number of hits matching the query. When `true`, the exact<br>number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. When `false`, the<br>response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.<br>Default is `10,000` hits.|
|» indices_boost|body|[object]|false|Boosts the `_score` of documents from specified indexes.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number|false|none|
|» docvalue_fields|body|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns doc values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|» min_score|body|number|false|Minimum `_score` for matching documents.<br>Documents with a lower `_score` are not included in the search results.|
|» post_filter|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» profile|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to return detailed timing information about the execution of individual components in a search request.<br>NOTE: This is a debugging tool and adds significant overhead to search execution.|
|» query|body|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|
|» script_fields|body|object|false|Retrieve a script evaluation (based on different fields) for each hit.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[_common___ScriptField](#schema_common___scriptfield)|false|The configuration for a script field.|
|» search_after|body|[_common___SortResults](#schema_common___sortresults)|false|none|
|» size|body|number|false|The number of hits to return.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|» slice|body|[_common___SlicedScroll](#schema_common___slicedscroll)|false|The configuration for a sliced scroll request.|
|» sort|body|[_common___Sort](#schema_common___sort)|false|none|
|» _source|body|[_core.search___SourceConfig](#schema_core.search___sourceconfig)|false|Defines how to fetch a source. Fetching can be disabled entirely, or the source can be filtered.|
|» fields|body|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|» suggest|body|[_core.search___Suggester](#schema_core.search___suggester)|false|none|
|» terminate_after|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.<br>If a query reaches this limit, OpenSearch terminates the query early.<br>OpenSearch collects documents before sorting.<br>Use with caution.<br>OpenSearch applies this parameter to each shard handling the request.<br>When possible, let OpenSearch perform early termination automatically.<br>Avoid specifying this parameter for requests that target data streams with backing indexes across multiple data tiers.<br>If set to `0` (default), the query does not terminate early.|
|» timeout|body|string|false|Specifies the period of time to wait for a response from each shard.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>Defaults to no timeout.|
|» track_scores|body|boolean|false|If `true`, calculate and return document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.|
|» version|body|boolean|false|If `true`, returns document version as part of a hit.|
|» seq_no_primary_term|body|boolean|false|If `true`, returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.|
|» stored_fields|body|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|» pit|body|[_core.search___PointInTimeReference](#schema_core.search___pointintimereference)|false|none|
|» stats|body|[string]|false|Stats groups to associate with the search.<br>Each group maintains a statistics aggregation for its associated searches.<br>You can retrieve these stats using the indexes stats API.|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_common___Id](#schema_common___id)|true|The ID of the rollup job.|
|if_primary_term|query|number|false|Only performs the operation if the document has the specified primary term.|
|if_seq_no|query|[_common___SequenceNumber](#schema_common___sequencenumber)|false|Only performs the operation if the document has the specified sequence number.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Whether to pretty-format the returned JSON response.|
|human|query|boolean|false|Whether to return human-readable values for statistics.|
|error_trace|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the stack trace of returned errors.|
|source|query|string|false|The URL-encoded request definition. Useful for libraries that do not accept a request body for non-POST requests.|
|filter_path|query|[_common___StringOrStringArray](#schema_common___stringorstringarray)|false|A comma-separated list of filters used to filter the response. Use wildcards to match any field or part of a field's name. To exclude fields, use `-`.|
|body|body|[rollups._common___RollupEntity](#schemarollups._common___rollupentity)|false|Updates the rollup job configuration.|
|» _id|body|[_common___Id](#schema_common___id)|false|The unique identifier for a resource.|
|» _seq_no|body|[_common___SequenceNumber](#schema_common___sequencenumber)|false|The sequence number of the document.|
|» _primary_term|body|integer(int64)|false|The primary term of the document.|
|» _version|body|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|
|» rollup|body|[rollups._common___Rollup](#schemarollups._common___rollup)|false|Defines the configuration for a rollup job.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|open_contexts|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of open search contexts.|
|query_current|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of currently running shard query operations.|
|query_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard query operations.|
|query_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard query operations, in milliseconds.|
|query_total|integer(int64)|true|none|The total number of shard query operations.|
|concurrent_query_total|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of query operations using concurrent segment search.|
|concurrent_query_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and `d` (days). Also accepts `0` without a unit and `-1` to indicate an unspecified value.|
|concurrent_query_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|false|none|The total amount of time taken by all query operations using concurrent segment search, in milliseconds.|
|concurrent_query_current|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of currently running query operations using concurrent segment search.|
|concurrent_avg_slice_count|number(double)|false|none|The average slice count of all search requests. This is computed as the total slice count divided by the total number of concurrent search requests.|
|fetch_current|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of currently running shard fetch operations.|
|fetch_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard fetch operations.|
|fetch_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard fetch operations, in milliseconds.|
|fetch_total|integer(int64)|true|none|The total number of shard fetch operations.|
|scroll_current|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of shard scroll operations that are currently running.|
|scroll_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard scroll operations.|
|scroll_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard scroll operations, in milliseconds.|
|scroll_total|integer(int64)|true|none|The total number of shard scroll operations.|
|point_in_time_total|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of shard Point in Time (PIT) contexts created (completed and active) since the node last restarted.|
|point_in_time_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and `d` (days). Also accepts `0` without a unit and `-1` to indicate an unspecified value.|
|point_in_time_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|false|none|The amount of time that shard PIT contexts have been held open since the node last restarted, in milliseconds.|
|point_in_time_current|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of currently open shard PIT contexts.|
|suggest_current|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of currently running shard suggest operations.|
|suggest_time|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|The total amount of time take to complete all shard suggest operations.|
|suggest_time_in_millis|[_common___UnitMillis](#schema_common___unitmillis)|true|none|The total amount of time taken to complete all shard suggest operations, in milliseconds.|
|suggest_total|integer(int64)|true|none|The total number of shard suggest operations.|
|search_idle_reactivate_count_total|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of idle search reactivations.|
|request|object|false|none|Statistics related to coordinator search operations for the node.|
|groups|object|false|none|The search statistics grouped by search groups.|

```json
{}
```

The absence of any type. This is commonly used in APIs that don't return a body.

Although "void" is generally used for a unit type that has only one value, this is interpreted as
the bottom type, which has no value. Most languages have a unit type, but few have a bottom type.

See https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_type and https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottom_type.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|background_filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|chi_square|[_common.aggregations___ChiSquareHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___chisquareheuristic)|false|none|none|
|exclude|[_common.aggregations___TermsExclude](#schema_common.aggregations___termsexclude)|false|none|none|
|execution_hint|[_common.aggregations___TermsAggregationExecutionHint](#schema_common.aggregations___termsaggregationexecutionhint)|false|none|none|
|field|[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)|false|none|The path to a field or an array of paths. Some APIs support wildcards in the path, which allows you to select multiple fields.|
|gnd|[_common.aggregations___GoogleNormalizedDistanceHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___googlenormalizeddistanceheuristic)|false|none|none|
|include|[_common.aggregations___TermsInclude](#schema_common.aggregations___termsinclude)|false|none|none|
|jlh|[_common___EmptyObject](#schema_common___emptyobject)|false|none|An empty object with no properties.|
|min_doc_count|integer(int64)|false|none|Only return terms that are found in more than `min_doc_count` hits.|
|mutual_information|[_common.aggregations___MutualInformationHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___mutualinformationheuristic)|false|none|none|
|percentage|[_common.aggregations___PercentageScoreHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___percentagescoreheuristic)|false|none|none|
|script_heuristic|[_common.aggregations___ScriptedHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___scriptedheuristic)|false|none|none|
|shard_min_doc_count|integer(int64)|false|none|Regulates the certainty a shard has if the term should actually be added to the candidate list or not with respect to the `min_doc_count`.<br>Terms will only be considered if their local shard frequency within the set is higher than the `shard_min_doc_count`.|
|shard_size|integer(int32)|false|none|Can be used to control the volumes of candidate terms produced by each shard.<br>By default, `shard_size` will be automatically estimated based on the number of shards and the `size` parameter.|
|size|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of buckets returned out of the overall terms list.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|execution_hint|global_ordinals|
|execution_hint|global_ordinals_hash|
|execution_hint|global_ordinals_low_cardinality|
|execution_hint|map|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|background_filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|chi_square|[_common.aggregations___ChiSquareHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___chisquareheuristic)|false|none|none|
|exclude|[_common.aggregations___TermsExclude](#schema_common.aggregations___termsexclude)|false|none|none|
|execution_hint|[_common.aggregations___TermsAggregationExecutionHint](#schema_common.aggregations___termsaggregationexecutionhint)|false|none|none|
|field|[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)|false|none|The path to a field or an array of paths. Some APIs support wildcards in the path, which allows you to select multiple fields.|
|filter_duplicate_text|boolean|false|none|Whether to out duplicate text to deal with noisy data.|
|gnd|[_common.aggregations___GoogleNormalizedDistanceHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___googlenormalizeddistanceheuristic)|false|none|none|
|include|[_common.aggregations___TermsInclude](#schema_common.aggregations___termsinclude)|false|none|none|
|jlh|[_common___EmptyObject](#schema_common___emptyobject)|false|none|An empty object with no properties.|
|min_doc_count|integer(int64)|false|none|Only return values that are found in more than `min_doc_count` hits.|
|mutual_information|[_common.aggregations___MutualInformationHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___mutualinformationheuristic)|false|none|none|
|percentage|[_common.aggregations___PercentageScoreHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___percentagescoreheuristic)|false|none|none|
|script_heuristic|[_common.aggregations___ScriptedHeuristic](#schema_common.aggregations___scriptedheuristic)|false|none|none|
|shard_min_doc_count|integer(int64)|false|none|Regulates the certainty a shard has if the values should actually be added to the candidate list or not with respect to the `min_doc_count`.<br>Values will only be considered if their local shard frequency within the set is higher than the `shard_min_doc_count`.|
|shard_size|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of candidate terms produced by each shard.<br>By default, `shard_size` will be automatically estimated based on the number of shards and the `size` parameter.|
|size|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of buckets returned out of the overall terms list.|
|source_fields|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|none|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|

|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS__common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsAggregate">_common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsAggregate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsaggregate"></a>
<a id="schema__common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsAggregate"></a>
<a id="tocS_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsaggregate"></a>
<a id="tocs_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsaggregate"></a>

```json
{
  "meta": {},
  "buckets": [
    {}
  ],
  "doc_count_error_upper_bound": 0,
  "sum_other_doc_count": 0
}
```

Result of a `terms` aggregation when the field is an `unsigned_long` (64-bit unsigned integer).
OpenSearch stores `unsigned_long` values as Long or BigInteger internally. In JSON responses,
bucket keys are represented as numbers, which may lose precision for values larger than 2^53--1
due to IEEE 754 double precision limitations. In protocol buffer representations, keys are
manually defined as uint64 to preserve the full 64-bit unsigned range. Use `key_as_string` in
buckets for exact string representation of large unsigned long values.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|sum_other_doc_count|integer(int64)|false|none|none|
|buckets|[[_common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsBucket](#schema_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsbucket)]|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS__common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsBucket">_common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsBucket</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsbucket"></a>
<a id="schema__common.aggregations___UnsignedLongTermsBucket"></a>
<a id="tocS_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsbucket"></a>
<a id="tocs_common.aggregations___unsignedlongtermsbucket"></a>

```json
{
  "doc_count_error_upper_bound": 0,
  "key": 0,
  "key_as_string": "string"
}
```

Terms bucket for `unsigned_long` field type. The server returns 64-bit unsigned integer values
as Long or BigInteger types. Due to JSON specification limitations (IEEE 754 double precision
provides only 53 bits of integer precision), the key is represented as `type: number` in the
OpenAPI spec. For protocol buffer definitions, this is manually overridden to `uint64` to
preserve the full 64-bit unsigned integer range in binary encoding.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|doc_count_error_upper_bound|integer(int64)|false|none|Upper bound of the document count error. Only present when `show_term_doc_count_error` is true.|
|key|number|true|none|The unsigned 64-bit integer bucket key. While JSON represents this as a number,<br>values larger than 2^53--1 may lose precision in JSON serialization. The gRPC<br>protocol buffer definition uses uint64 to preserve full precision. Use `key_as_string`<br>for exact string representation of large values.<br>|
|key_as_string|string|false|none|String representation of the key. Only present when a custom `format` parameter is specified in the aggregation request.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer) \| [[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must appear in matching documents.<br>However, unlike `must`, the score of the query will be ignored.|
|minimum_should_match|[_common___MinimumShouldMatch](#schema_common___minimumshouldmatch)|false|none|The minimum number of terms that should match as an integer, percentage, or range.|
|must|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer) \| [[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must appear in matching documents and will contribute to the score.|
|must_not|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer) \| [[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must not appear in the matching documents.<br>Because scoring is ignored, a score of `0` is returned for all documents.|
|should|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer) \| [[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) should appear in the matching document.|
|adjust_pure_negative|boolean|false|none|Ensures correct behavior when a query contains only `must_not` clauses.<br>By default set to true, OpenSearch adds a match-all clause to ensure results are returned from Lucene, with the `must_not` conditions applied as filters.<br>If set to false, the query may return no results, as Lucene typically requires at least one positive condition.|

|_name|string|false|none|none|

|positive|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|fields|[[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)]|true|none|List of fields to search. Field wildcard patterns are allowed. Only `text` fields are supported, and they must all have the same search `analyzer`.|
|query|string|true|none|Text to search for in the provided `fields`.<br>The `combined_fields` query analyzes the provided text before performing a search.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|operator|[_common.query_dsl___CombinedFieldsOperator](#schema_common.query_dsl___combinedfieldsoperator)|false|none|none|
|minimum_should_match|[_common___MinimumShouldMatch](#schema_common___minimumshouldmatch)|false|none|The minimum number of terms that should match as an integer, percentage, or range.|
|zero_terms_query|[_common.query_dsl___CombinedFieldsZeroTerms](#schema_common.query_dsl___combinedfieldszeroterms)|false|none|none|

OpenSearch accepts both as an input but will generally output a string.<br>representation.|
|scale|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|true|none|A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and `d` (days). Also accepts `0` without a unit and `-1` to indicate an unspecified value.|

|min_children|integer(int32)|false|none|Minimum number of child documents that match the query required to match the query for a returned parent document.<br>If the parent document does not meet this limit, it is excluded from the search results.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|true|none|none|
|score_mode|[_common.query_dsl___ChildScoreMode](#schema_common.query_dsl___childscoremode)|false|none|none|
|type|[_common___RelationName](#schema_common___relationname)|true|none|The name of a relation in a join field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|score_mode|avg|
|score_mode|max|
|score_mode|min|
|score_mode|none|
|score_mode|sum|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|ignore_unmapped|[_common.query_dsl___IgnoreUnmapped](#schema_common.query_dsl___ignoreunmapped)|false|none|Indicates whether to ignore an unmapped `parent_type` and not return any documents instead of an error.<br>You can use this parameter to query multiple indexes that may not contain the `parent_type`.|
|inner_hits|[_core.search___InnerHits](#schema_core.search___innerhits)|false|none|none|
|parent_type|[_common___RelationName](#schema_common___relationname)|true|none|The name of a relation in a join field.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|true|none|none|
|score|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the relevance score of a matching parent document is aggregated into its child documents.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|ignore_unmapped|[_common.query_dsl___IgnoreUnmapped](#schema_common.query_dsl___ignoreunmapped)|false|none|Indicates whether to ignore an unmapped path and not return any documents instead of an error.|
|inner_hits|[_core.search___InnerHits](#schema_core.search___innerhits)|false|none|none|
|path|[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)|true|none|The path to a field or an array of paths. Some APIs support wildcards in the path, which allows you to select multiple fields.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|true|none|none|
|score_mode|[_common.query_dsl___ChildScoreMode](#schema_common.query_dsl___childscoremode)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|score_mode|avg|
|score_mode|max|
|score_mode|min|
|score_mode|none|
|score_mode|sum|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|allow_leading_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the wildcard characters `*` and `?` are allowed as the first character of the query string.|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert text in the query string into tokens.|
|analyze_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|default_field|[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)|false|none|The path to a field or an array of paths. Some APIs support wildcards in the path, which allows you to select multiple fields.|
|default_operator|[_common.query_dsl___Operator](#schema_common.query_dsl___operator)|false|none|none|
|enable_position_increments|boolean|false|none|If `true`, enable position increments in queries constructed from a `query_string` search.|
|escape|boolean|false|none|none|
|fields|[[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)]|false|none|Array of fields to search. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|fuzziness|[_common___Fuzziness](#schema_common___fuzziness)|false|none|none|
|fuzzy_max_expansions|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query expands for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_prefix_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_rewrite|[_common___MultiTermQueryRewrite](#schema_common___multitermqueryrewrite)|false|none|none|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|max_determinized_states|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of automaton states required for the query.|
|minimum_should_match|[_common___MinimumShouldMatch](#schema_common___minimumshouldmatch)|false|none|The minimum number of terms that should match as an integer, percentage, or range.|
|phrase_slop|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of positions allowed between matching tokens for phrases.|
|query|string|true|none|Query string you wish to parse and use for search.|
|quote_analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert quoted text in the query string into tokens.<br>For quoted text, this parameter overrides the analyzer specified in the `analyzer` parameter.|
|quote_field_suffix|string|false|none|Suffix appended to quoted text in the query string.<br>You can use this suffix to use a different analysis method for exact matches.|
|rewrite|[_common___MultiTermQueryRewrite](#schema_common___multitermqueryrewrite)|false|none|none|
|tie_breaker|number(float)|false|none|How to combine the queries generated from the individual search terms in the resulting `dis_max` query.|
|time_zone|[_common___TimeZone](#schema_common___timezone)|false|none|The time zone identifier.|
|type|[_common.query_dsl___TextQueryType](#schema_common.query_dsl___textquerytype)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number(float)|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert text in the query string into tokens.|
|analyze_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the parser creates a `match_phrase` query for each multi-position token.|
|default_operator|[_common.query_dsl___Operator](#schema_common.query_dsl___operator)|false|none|none|
|fields|[[_common___Field](#schema_common___field)]|false|none|Array of fields you wish to search.<br>Accepts wildcard expressions.<br>You also can boost relevance scores for matches to particular fields using a caret (`^`) notation.<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field index` setting, which has a default value of `*`.|
|flags|[_common.query_dsl___SimpleQueryStringFlags](#schema_common.query_dsl___simplequerystringflags)|false|none|Query flags can be either a single flag or a combination of flags (e.g. `OR\|AND\|PREFIX`).|
|fuzzy_max_expansions|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query expands for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_prefix_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|minimum_should_match|[_common___MinimumShouldMatch](#schema_common___minimumshouldmatch)|false|none|The minimum number of terms that should match as an integer, percentage, or range.|
|query|string|true|none|Query string in the simple query string syntax you wish to parse and use for search.|
|quote_field_suffix|string|false|none|Suffix appended to quoted text in the query string.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|default_operator|and|
|default_operator|AND|
|default_operator|or|
|default_operator|OR|

|hits|[[_core.rank_eval___RankEvalHitItem](#schema_core.rank_eval___rankevalhititem)]|true|none|The `hits` section provides a grouping of the search results with their supplied ratings.|
|metric_details|object|true|none|The `metric_details` section provides additional information about the calculated quality metric indicating the number of relevant retrieved documents. The content varies for each metric but allows for better interpretation of the results.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|[_common___Indices](#schema_common___indices)|true|none|A comma-separated list of data streams, indexes, and aliases used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indexes, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|remote|[_core.reindex___RemoteSource](#schema_core.reindex___remotesource)|false|none|none|
|size|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of documents to index per batch.<br>Use the `size` setting when indexing from a remote cluster. This ensures that batches fit in the on-heap buffer. The buffer defaults to a maximum size of `100MB`.|
|slice|[_common___SlicedScroll](#schema_common___slicedscroll)|false|none|The configuration for a sliced scroll request.|
|sort|[_common___Sort](#schema_common___sort)|false|none|none|
|_source|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|none|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|

|max_fragment_length|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|max_analyzer_offset|integer(int32)|false|none|If set to a non-negative value, highlighting stops at this defined maximum limit.<br>The rest of the text is not processed or highlighted, and no error is returned.<br>The `max_analyzer_offset` query setting does not override the `index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset` setting, which takes precedence when it is set to a lower value than the query setting.|
|no_match_size|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of text you want to return from the beginning of the field if there are no matching fragments to highlight.|
|number_of_fragments|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of fragments to return.<br>When the number of fragments is set to `0`, no fragments are returned.<br>Instead, the entirety of a field's contents are highlighted and returned.<br>This is useful when you need to highlight short texts, such as a title or address, in which fragmentation is not required.<br>If `number_of_fragments` is set to `0`, the `fragment_size` is ignored.|
|options|object|false|none|none|
|order|[_core.search___HighlighterOrder](#schema_core.search___highlighterorder)|false|none|none|
|phrase_limit|integer(int32)|false|none|Controls the number of matching phrases in a document that are considered.<br>This prevents the `fvh` highlighter from analyzing too many phrases and consuming too much memory.<br>When using `matched_fields`, phrase-limited phrases per matched field are considered. Raising the limit increases the query time and consumes more memory.<br>This setting is only supported by the `fvh` highlighter.|
|post_tags|[string]|false|none|When used in conjunction with `pre_tags`, defines the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|pre_tags|[string]|false|none|When used in conjunction with `post_tags`, defines the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|require_field_match|boolean|false|none|By default, only fields that contains a query match are highlighted.<br>Set to `false` to highlight all fields.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|[_core.search___HighlighterType](#schema_core.search___highlightertype)|false|none|none|
|boundary_chars|string|false|none|A string that contains each boundary character.|
|boundary_max_scan|integer(int32)|false|none|How far to scan for boundary characters.|
|boundary_scanner|[_core.search___BoundaryScanner](#schema_core.search___boundaryscanner)|false|none|none|
|boundary_scanner_locale|string|false|none|Controls which locale is used to search for sentence and word boundaries.<br>This parameter takes the form of a language tag, for example, `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"`, or `"ja-JP"`.|
|force_source|boolean|false|none|none|
|fragmenter|[_core.search___HighlighterFragmenter](#schema_core.search___highlighterfragmenter)|false|none|none|
|fragment_offset|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|fragment_size|integer(int32)|false|none|The size of the highlighted fragment in characters.|
|highlight_filter|boolean|false|none|none|
|highlight_query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|max_fragment_length|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|max_analyzer_offset|integer(int32)|false|none|If set to a non-negative value, highlighting stops at this defined maximum limit.<br>The rest of the text is not processed or highlighted, and no error is returned.<br>The `max_analyzer_offset` query setting does not override the `index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset` setting, which takes precedence when it is set to a lower value than the query setting.|
|no_match_size|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of text you want to return from the beginning of the field if there are no matching fragments to highlight.|
|number_of_fragments|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of fragments to return.<br>When the number of fragments is set to `0`, no fragments are returned.<br>Instead, the entirety of a field's contents are highlighted and returned.<br>This is useful when you need to highlight short texts, such as a title or address, in which fragmentation is not required.<br>If `number_of_fragments` is set to `0`, the `fragment_size` is ignored.|
|options|object|false|none|none|
|order|[_core.search___HighlighterOrder](#schema_core.search___highlighterorder)|false|none|none|
|phrase_limit|integer(int32)|false|none|Controls the number of matching phrases in a document that are considered.<br>This prevents the `fvh` highlighter from analyzing too many phrases and consuming too much memory.<br>When using `matched_fields`, phrase-limited phrases per matched field are considered. Raising the limit increases the query time and consumes more memory.<br>This setting is only supported by the `fvh` highlighter.|
|post_tags|[string]|false|none|When used in conjunction with `pre_tags`, defines the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|pre_tags|[string]|false|none|When used in conjunction with `post_tags`, defines the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|require_field_match|boolean|false|none|By default, only fields that contains a query match are highlighted.<br>Set to `false` to highlight all fields.|
|tags_schema|[_core.search___HighlighterTagsSchema](#schema_core.search___highlightertagsschema)|false|none|none|

```json
true
```

The number of hits matching the query. When `true`, the exact
number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. When `false`, the
response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.
Default is `10,000` hits.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|boolean|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|integer(int32)|false|none|none|

```json
{
  "max_doc_freq": 0,
  "max_num_terms": 0,
  "max_term_freq": 0,
  "max_word_length": 0,
  "min_doc_freq": 0,
  "min_term_freq": 0,
  "min_word_length": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_doc_freq|integer(int32)|false|none|Ignores words that appear in more than the specified number of documents.<br>Default is `unbounded`.|
|max_num_terms|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of terms that should be returned per field.|
|max_term_freq|integer(int32)|false|none|Ignore words with more than this frequency in the source doc.<br>Default is `unbounded`.|
|max_word_length|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum word length.<br>Words longer than this value will be ignored.<br>Default is `unbounded`.|
|min_doc_freq|integer(int32)|false|none|Ignore terms which do not occur in at least this many docs.|
|min_term_freq|integer(int32)|false|none|Ignore words with less than this frequency in the source doc.|
|min_word_length|integer(int32)|false|none|The minimum word length.<br>Words shorter than this value will be ignored.<br>Default is 0.|

The search definition using the Query DSL.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Defines the aggregations that are run as part of the search request.|
|collapse|[_core.search___FieldCollapse](#schema_core.search___fieldcollapse)|false|none|none|
|explain|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.|
|ext|object|false|none|Configuration of search extensions defined by OpenSearch plugins.|
|from|number|false|none|Starting document offset.<br>Needs to be non-negative.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|highlight|[_core.search___Highlight](#schema_core.search___highlight)|false|none|none|
|track_total_hits|[_core.search___TrackHits](#schema_core.search___trackhits)|false|none|The number of hits matching the query. When `true`, the exact<br>number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. When `false`, the<br>response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.<br>Default is `10,000` hits.|
|indices_boost|[object]|false|none|Boosts the `_score` of documents from specified indexes.|
|docvalue_fields|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns doc values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|min_score|number|false|none|Minimum `_score` for matching documents.<br>Documents with a lower `_score` are not included in the search results.|
|post_filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|profile|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to return detailed timing information about the execution of individual components in a search request.<br>NOTE: This is a debugging tool and adds significant overhead to search execution.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|script_fields|object|false|none|Retrieve a script evaluation (based on different fields) for each hit.|
|search_after|[_common___SortResults](#schema_common___sortresults)|false|none|none|
|size|number|false|none|The number of hits to return.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|slice|[_common___SlicedScroll](#schema_common___slicedscroll)|false|none|The configuration for a sliced scroll request.|
|sort|[_common___Sort](#schema_common___sort)|false|none|none|
|_source|[_core.search___SourceConfig](#schema_core.search___sourceconfig)|false|none|Defines how to fetch a source. Fetching can be disabled entirely, or the source can be filtered.|
|fields|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|suggest|[_core.search___Suggester](#schema_core.search___suggester)|false|none|none|
|terminate_after|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.<br>If a query reaches this limit, OpenSearch terminates the query early.<br>OpenSearch collects documents before sorting.<br>Use with caution.<br>OpenSearch applies this parameter to each shard handling the request.<br>When possible, let OpenSearch perform early termination automatically.<br>Avoid specifying this parameter for requests that target data streams with backing indexes across multiple data tiers.<br>If set to `0` (default), the query does not terminate early.|
|timeout|string|false|none|Specifies the period of time to wait for a response from each shard.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>Defaults to no timeout.|
|track_scores|boolean|false|none|If `true`, calculate and return document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.|
|version|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns document version as part of a hit.|
|seq_no_primary_term|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.|
|stored_fields|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|none|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|pit|[_core.search___PointInTimeReference](#schema_core.search___pointintimereference)|false|none|none|
|stats|[string]|false|none|Stats groups to associate with the search.<br>Each group maintains a statistics aggregation for its associated searches.<br>You can retrieve these stats using the indexes stats API.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|shards|string|false|none|Number of primary and replica shards assigned to the node.|
|disk.indices|null \| string|false|none|Disk space used by the node's shards. Does not include disk space for the translog or unassigned shards.<br>IMPORTANT: This metric double-counts disk space for hard-linked files, such as those created when shrinking, splitting, or cloning an index.|
|disk.used|null \| string|false|none|Total disk space in use.<br>OpenSearch retrieves this metric from the node's operating system (OS).<br>The metric includes disk space for: OpenSearch, including the translog and unassigned shards; the node's operating system; any other applications or files on the node.<br>Unlike `disk.indices`, this metric does not double-count disk space for hard-linked files.|
|disk.avail|null \| string|false|none|Free disk space available to OpenSearch.<br>OpenSearch retrieves this metric from the node's operating system.<br>Disk-based shard allocation uses this metric to assign shards to nodes based on available disk space.|
|disk.total|null \| string|false|none|Total disk space for the node, including in-use and available space.|
|disk.percent|[_common___PercentageString](#schema_common___percentagestring) \| null|false|none|Total percentage of disk space in use. Calculated as `disk.used / disk.total`.|
|host|[_common___Host](#schema_common___host) \| null|false|none|Network host for the node. Set using the `network.host` setting.|
|ip|[_common___Ip](#schema_common___ip) \| null|false|none|IP address and port for the node.|
|node|string|false|none|Name for the node. Set using the `node.name` setting.|

|version|[_common___VersionString](#schema_common___versionstring)|false|none|none|
|compound|string|false|none|If `true`, the segment is stored in a compound file.<br>This means Lucene merged all files from the segment in a single file to save file descriptors.|

|unassigned.reason|null \| string|false|none|The reason for the last change to the state of an unassigned shard.<br>It does not explain why the shard is currently unassigned; use the cluster allocation explain API for that information.<br>Returned values include:<br>`ALLOCATION_FAILED`: Unassigned as a result of a failed allocation of the shard.<br>`CLUSTER_RECOVERED`: Unassigned as a result of a full cluster recovery.<br>`DANGLING_INDEX_IMPORTED`: Unassigned as a result of importing a dangling index.<br>`EXISTING_INDEX_RESTORED`: Unassigned as a result of restoring into a closed index.<br>`FORCED_EMPTY_PRIMARY`: The shard's allocation was last modified by forcing an empty primary using the cluster reroute API.<br>`INDEX_CLOSED`: Unassigned because the index was closed.<br>`INDEX_CREATED`: Unassigned as a result of an API creation of an index.<br>`INDEX_REOPENED`: Unassigned as a result of opening a closed index.<br>`MANUAL_ALLOCATION`: The shard's allocation was last modified by the cluster reroute API.<br>`NEW_INDEX_RESTORED`: Unassigned as a result of restoring into a new index.<br>`NODE_LEFT`: Unassigned as a result of the node hosting it leaving the cluster.<br>`NODE_RESTARTING`: Similar to `NODE_LEFT`, except that the node was registered as restarting using the node shutdown API.<br>`PRIMARY_FAILED`: The shard was initializing as a replica, but the primary shard failed before the initialization completed.<br>`REALLOCATED_REPLICA`: A better replica location is identified and causes the existing replica allocation to be cancelled.<br>`REINITIALIZED`: When a shard moves from started back to initializing.<br>`REPLICA_ADDED`: Unassigned as a result of explicit addition of a replica.<br>`REROUTE_CANCELLED`: Unassigned as a result of explicit cancel reroute command.|
|unassigned.at|null \| string|false|none|The time at which the shard became unassigned in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|unassigned.for|null \| string|false|none|The time at which the shard was requested to be unassigned in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|unassigned.details|null \| string|false|none|Additional details as to why the shard became unassigned.<br>It does not explain why the shard is not assigned; use the cluster allocation explain API for that information.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the snapshot.|
|repository|string|false|none|The repository name.|
|status|string|false|none|The state of the snapshot process.<br>Returned values include:<br>`FAILED`: The snapshot process failed.<br>`INCOMPATIBLE`: The snapshot process is incompatible with the current cluster version.<br>`IN_PROGRESS`: The snapshot process started but has not completed.<br>`PARTIAL`: The snapshot process completed with a partial success.<br>`SUCCESS`: The snapshot process completed with a full success.|
|start_epoch|[_common___StringifiedEpochTimeUnitSeconds](#schema_common___stringifiedepochtimeunitseconds)|false|none|Certain APIs may return values, including numbers such as epoch timestamps, as strings. This setting captures<br>this behavior while keeping the semantics of the field type.<br><br>Depending on the target language, code generators can keep the union or remove it and leniently parse<br>strings to the target type.|
|start_time|[_common___TimeOfDay](#schema_common___timeofday)|false|none|Time of day, expressed as HH:MM:SS.|
|end_epoch|[_common___StringifiedEpochTimeUnitSeconds](#schema_common___stringifiedepochtimeunitseconds)|false|none|Certain APIs may return values, including numbers such as epoch timestamps, as strings. This setting captures<br>this behavior while keeping the semantics of the field type.<br><br>Depending on the target language, code generators can keep the union or remove it and leniently parse<br>strings to the target type.|
|end_time|[_common___TimeOfDay](#schema_common___timeofday)|false|none|Time of day, expressed as HH:MM:SS.|
|duration|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and `d` (days). Also accepts `0` without a unit and `-1` to indicate an unspecified value.|
|indices|string|false|none|The number of indexes in the snapshot.|
|successful_shards|string|false|none|The number of successful shards in the snapshot.|
|failed_shards|string|false|none|The number of failed shards in the snapshot.|
|total_shards|string|false|none|The total number of shards in the snapshot.|
|reason|string|false|none|The reason for any snapshot failures.|

<h2 id="tocS_cluster._common___WaitForNodes">cluster._common___WaitForNodes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacluster._common___waitfornodes"></a>
<a id="schema_cluster._common___WaitForNodes"></a>
<a id="tocScluster._common___waitfornodes"></a>
<a id="tocscluster._common___waitfornodes"></a>

```json
0
```

Waits until the specified number of nodes (`N`) is available. Accepts `>=N`, `<=N`, `>N`, and `<N`. You can also use `ge(N)`, `le(N)`, `gt(N)`, and `lt(N)` notation.

{
  "cancel": {

  },

  },

    "index": "string",
    "shard": 0,
    "node": "string"
  },
  "allocate_stale_primary": {
    "index": "string",
    "shard": 0,

  },

  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cancel|[cluster.reroute___CommandCancelAction](#schemacluster.reroute___commandcancelaction)|false|none|Cancel allocation of a shard (or recovery). Accepts `index` and `shard` for index<br>name and shard number, and `node` for the node to cancel the shard allocation<br>on. This can be used to force resynchronization of existing replicas from the<br>primary shard by cancelling them and allowing them to be reinitialized<br>through the standard recovery process. By default only replica shard<br>allocations can be cancelled. If it is necessary to cancel the allocation of<br>a primary shard then the `allow_primary` flag must also be included in the<br>request.|
|move|[cluster.reroute___CommandMoveAction](#schemacluster.reroute___commandmoveaction)|false|none|Move a started shard from one node to another node. Accepts `index` and `shard`<br>for index name and shard number, `from_node` for the node to move the shard<br>from, and `to_node` for the node to move the shard to.|
|allocate_replica|[cluster.reroute___CommandAllocateReplicaAction](#schemacluster.reroute___commandallocatereplicaaction)|false|none|Allocate an unassigned replica shard to a node. Accepts `index` and `shard` for<br>index name and shard number, and `node` to allocate the shard to. Takes<br>allocation deciders into account.|
|allocate_stale_primary|[cluster.reroute___CommandAllocatePrimaryAction](#schemacluster.reroute___commandallocateprimaryaction)|false|none|Allocate a primary shard to a node that holds a stale copy. Accepts `index`<br>and `shard` for index name and shard number, and `node` to allocate the shard to.<br>Using this command may lead to data loss for the provided shard id. If a node<br>which has the good copy of the data rejoins the cluster later on, that data<br>will be deleted or overwritten with the data of the stale copy that was<br>forcefully allocated with this command. To ensure that these implications are<br>well-understood, this command requires the flag `accept_data_loss` to be<br>explicitly set to true.|
|allocate_empty_primary|[cluster.reroute___CommandAllocatePrimaryAction](#schemacluster.reroute___commandallocateprimaryaction)|false|none|Allocate an empty primary shard to a node. Accepts `index` and `shard` for<br>index name and shard number, and `node` to allocate the shard to. Using this<br>command leads to a complete loss of all data that was indexed into this<br>shard, if it was previously started. If a node which has a copy of the data<br>rejoins the cluster later on, that data will be deleted. To ensure that these<br>implications are well-understood, this command requires the flag<br>`accept_data_loss` to be explicitly set to true.|

The index alias configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|index_routing|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|none|The routing value for the document.|
|is_hidden|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the alias is hidden.<br>All indexes for the alias must have the same `is_hidden` value.|
|is_write_index|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the index is the write index for the alias.|
|routing|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|none|The routing value for the document.|
|search_routing|[_common___Routing](#schema_common___routing)|false|none|The routing value for the document.|

```

The configuration for an index alias.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|index_routing|string|false|none|The value used to route indexing operations to a specific shard.<br>When specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for indexing operations.|
|is_write_index|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the index is the write index for the alias.|
|routing|string|false|none|The value used to route indexing and search operations to a specific shard.|
|search_routing|string|false|none|The value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>When specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for search operations.|
|is_hidden|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the alias is hidden.<br>All indexes for the alias must have the same `is_hidden` value.|

"fs"
```

The type of storage implementation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Uses the default file system implementation.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Uses a hybrid of memory-mapped and regular file system implementation.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Uses memory-mapped file system implementation.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Uses NIO file system implementation.|

```

The configuration for an index template.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_patterns|[_common___Names](#schema_common___names)|true|none|A comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve. Supports wildcards (`*`).  To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|composed_of|[[_common___Name](#schema_common___name)]|false|none|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|template|[indices._common___IndexTemplateSummary](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatesummary)|false|none|The summary configuration for an index template.|
|version|[_common___VersionNumber](#schema_common___versionnumber)|false|none|none|
|priority|integer(int64)|false|none|The priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by OpenSearch.|
|_meta|[_common___Metadata](#schema_common___metadata)|false|none|The custom metadata attached to a resource.|
|allow_auto_create|boolean|false|none|Whether the template allows automatic index creation.|
|data_stream|[indices._common___IndexTemplateDataStreamConfiguration](#schemaindices._common___indextemplatedatastreamconfiguration)|false|none|The data stream configuration for an index template.|

The data stream configuration for an index template.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hidden|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the data stream is hidden.|
|allow_custom_routing|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the data stream supports custom routing.|
|timestamp_field|[indices._common___DataStreamTimestampField](#schemaindices._common___datastreamtimestampfield)|false|none|The timestamp field configuration for a data stream.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._common___Translog">indices._common___Translog</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._common___translog"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._common___Translog"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._common___translog"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._common___translog"></a>

```json
{
  "sync_interval": "string",
  "durability": "ASYNC",
  "flush_threshold_size": "string",
  "generation_threshold_size": "string",
  "retention": {
    "size": "string",
    "age": "string"
  }
}
```

The translog configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sync_interval|[_common___Duration](#schema_common___duration)|false|none|A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and `d` (days). Also accepts `0` without a unit and `-1` to indicate an unspecified value.|
|durability|[indices._common___TranslogDurability](#schemaindices._common___translogdurability)|false|none|The durability settings for the translog.|
|flush_threshold_size|[_common___HumanReadableByteCount](#schema_common___humanreadablebytecount)|false|none|The unique identifier of a node.|
|generation_threshold_size|[_common___HumanReadableByteCount](#schema_common___humanreadablebytecount)|false|none|The unique identifier of a node.|
|retention|[indices._common___TranslogRetention](#schemaindices._common___translogretention)|false|none|The retention configuration for the translog.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._common___TranslogDurability">indices._common___TranslogDurability</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._common___translogdurability"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._common___TranslogDurability"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._common___translogdurability"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._common___translogdurability"></a>

```json
"ASYNC"
```

The durability settings for the translog.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Asynchronous durability - acknowledges write operations after they are written to memory.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Request durability - acknowledges write operations after they are written to disk.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Asynchronous durability (lowercase variant).|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Request durability (lowercase variant).|

<h2 id="tocS_indices.stats___ShardSequenceNumber">indices.stats___ShardSequenceNumber</h2>

<a id="tocsindices.stats___shardsequencenumber"></a>

```json
{
  "global_checkpoint": 0,
  "local_checkpoint": 0,
  "max_seq_no": 0
}
```

The sequence number information for a shard.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|global_checkpoint|integer(int64)|true|none|The global checkpoint for the shard.|
|local_checkpoint|integer(int64)|true|none|The local checkpoint for the shard.|
|max_seq_no|[_common___SequenceNumber](#schema_common___sequencenumber)|true|none|The sequence number of the document.|

The action to perform on aliases.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add|[indices.update_aliases___AddAction](#schemaindices.update_aliases___addaction)|false|none|The configuration for adding an alias.|
|remove|[indices.update_aliases___RemoveAction](#schemaindices.update_aliases___removeaction)|false|none|The configuration for removing an alias.|
|remove_index|[indices.update_aliases___RemoveIndexAction](#schemaindices.update_aliases___removeindexaction)|false|none|The configuration for removing an index.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Defines the aggregations that are run as part of the search request.|
|collapse|[_core.search___FieldCollapse](#schema_core.search___fieldcollapse)|false|none|none|
|explain|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.|
|ext|object|false|none|Configuration of search extensions defined by OpenSearch plugins.|
|from|number|false|none|Starting document offset.<br>Needs to be non-negative.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|highlight|[_core.search___Highlight](#schema_core.search___highlight)|false|none|none|
|track_total_hits|[_core.search___TrackHits](#schema_core.search___trackhits)|false|none|The number of hits matching the query. When `true`, the exact<br>number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. When `false`, the<br>response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.<br>Default is `10,000` hits.|
|indices_boost|[object]|false|none|Boosts the `_score` of documents from specified indexes.|
|docvalue_fields|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns doc values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|min_score|number|false|none|Minimum `_score` for matching documents.<br>Documents with a lower `_score` are not included in the search results.|
|post_filter|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|profile|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to return detailed timing information about the execution of individual components in a search request.<br>NOTE: This is a debugging tool and adds significant overhead to search execution.|
|query|[_common.query_dsl___QueryContainer](#schema_common.query_dsl___querycontainer)|false|none|none|
|script_fields|object|false|none|Retrieve a script evaluation (based on different fields) for each hit.|
|search_after|[_common___SortResults](#schema_common___sortresults)|false|none|none|
|size|number|false|none|The number of hits to return.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|slice|[_common___SlicedScroll](#schema_common___slicedscroll)|false|none|The configuration for a sliced scroll request.|
|sort|[_common___Sort](#schema_common___sort)|false|none|none|
|_source|[_core.search___SourceConfig](#schema_core.search___sourceconfig)|false|none|Defines how to fetch a source. Fetching can be disabled entirely, or the source can be filtered.|
|fields|[[_common.query_dsl___FieldAndFormat](#schema_common.query_dsl___fieldandformat)]|false|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) patterns.<br>The request returns values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|suggest|[_core.search___Suggester](#schema_core.search___suggester)|false|none|none|
|terminate_after|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.<br>If a query reaches this limit, OpenSearch terminates the query early.<br>OpenSearch collects documents before sorting.<br>Use with caution.<br>OpenSearch applies this parameter to each shard handling the request.<br>When possible, let OpenSearch perform early termination automatically.<br>Avoid specifying this parameter for requests that target data streams with backing indexes across multiple data tiers.<br>If set to `0` (default), the query does not terminate early.|
|timeout|string|false|none|Specifies the period of time to wait for a response from each shard.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>Defaults to no timeout.|
|track_scores|boolean|false|none|If `true`, calculate and return document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.|
|version|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns document version as part of a hit.|
|seq_no_primary_term|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.|
|stored_fields|[_common___Fields](#schema_common___fields)|false|none|A comma-separated list or a wildcard expression specifying the fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|pit|[_core.search___PointInTimeReference](#schema_core.search___pointintimereference)|false|none|none|
|stats|[string]|false|none|Stats groups to associate with the search.<br>Each group maintains a statistics aggregation for its associated searches.<br>You can retrieve these stats using the indexes stats API.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|control_group|string|false|none|The `memory` control group to which the OpenSearch process belongs.|
|limit_in_bytes|string|false|none|The maximum amount of user memory (including file cache) allowed for all tasks in the same cgroup as the OpenSearch process.<br>This value can be too big to store in a `long`, so is returned as a string so that the value returned can exactly match what the underlying operating system interface returns.<br>Any value that is too large to parse into a `long` almost certainly means no limit has been set for the cgroup.|
|usage_in_bytes|string|false|none|The total current memory usage by processes in the cgroup, in bytes, by all tasks in the same cgroup as the OpenSearch process.<br>This value is stored as a string for consistency with `limit_in_bytes`.|

Defines the configuration for a rollup job.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rollup_id|string|false|none|The ID for the rollup job.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the rollup job is enabled.|
|schedule|[rollups._common___Schedule](#schemarollups._common___schedule)|false|none|Defines the execution schedule for a rollup job.|
|last_updated_time|number|false|none|When the rollup job was last updated.|
|enabled_time|number|false|none|When the rollup job was enabled.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the rollup job.|
|schema_version|number|false|none|The schema version for the rollup job.|
|source_index|string|false|none|The source index pattern for the rollup job.|
|target_index|string|false|none|The target index where rollup results are stored.|
|target_index_settings|[indices._common___IndexSettings](#schemaindices._common___indexsettings)|false|none|The configuration settings for an index.|
|metadata_id|null \| string|false|none|The metadata ID associated with the rollup job.|
|page_size|number|false|none|The number of documents to process per iteration.|
|delay|number|false|none|The time delay in milliseconds between consecutive rollup executions.|
|continuous|boolean|false|none|Whether the rollup job runs continuously.|
|dimensions|[[rollups._common___DimensionsConfigItem](#schemarollups._common___dimensionsconfigitem)]|false|none|The dimensions to aggregate data in the rollup.|
|metrics|[[rollups._common___MetricsConfigItem](#schemarollups._common___metricsconfigitem)]|false|none|The metrics to calculate in the rollup.|
|error_notification|string|false|none|Set up a Mustache message template for error notifications. For example, if an index rollup job fails, the system can send  a message to a Slack channel.|
